paper_metadata.title: Optimal Tuning of Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks for Multivariate Distribution Loading

summary: The paper studies hyperparameter tuning for gate‑based qGANs that load lognormal distributions into quantum states. Using 3‑qubit circuits with Adam AMSGRAD and optimized settings, the authors reduce the Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistic to about 0.0296 ± 0.0149 compared to a previous benchmark of 0.0821 (≈64% improvement), while training on ~17,200 samples. Experiments are performed on noiseless Qiskit simulators with 3–4 qubits and show that Adam significantly outperforms SPSA in approximation accuracy.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum generative adversarial network (qGAN) for loading and approximating univariate and multivariate lognormal distributions, with hyperparameter tuning of generator/discriminator learning rates, network sizes, shot counts, and optimizer choice (Adam AMSGRAD vs SPSA).

algorithm.variant: qGAN for approximate data loading / distribution learning
algorithm.ansatz: Layered variational circuit with RY rotations and circular CZ entanglement
algorithm.convergence_criteria: run converges when generator parameters are substantially stable for m = M/200 subsequent epochs; slope threshold 1/10 of generator learning rate
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initialization of generator and discriminator parameters; multiple random seeds / initial conditions
algorithm.hyperparameters.discriminator_hidden_lay: (H1,H2) baseline = (8,8); sensitivity analysis performed over H1,H2 ∈ {4,8,16,32,64,128,256}

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Generator outputs amplitudes x_i whose squared magnitudes encode approximate probabilities; univariate distribution discretized into 2^n bins, and multivariate distributions are treated equivalently by feeding each qubit as an input node to the discriminator
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize divergence between target distribution p_i and generated distribution \tilde{p}_i via adversarial training; evaluation uses chi-square goodness-of-fit and Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Implicit normalization of output probabilities through quantum state amplitudes; no explicit penalty terms reported

problem_instance.description: Approximate loading of a lognormal distribution for data loading / distribution learning; paper emphasizes equivalence of univariate and multivariate distributions under the discriminator design

dataset_specification.description: Lognormal with mu=1, sigma=1, discretized in [0,8] into 2^n bins

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Samples are binned into 2^n buckets over [0,8]; tails are trimmed, reducing sample count to ~17,200
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each test case repeated 10 times with different random initializations; quality assessed with chi-square test p-values, and also Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic / relative entropy for comparison with prior work

noise_model.noise_type: noiseless simulator used for training; statevector simulator used for final evaluation

implementation_details.framework_version: Qiskit 0.1x / PyTorch 1.8.1 referenced; exact version not fully specified
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Training data shuffled and split into batches; discriminator input uses one node per qubit rather than one node per label
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: After training, circuit evaluated on statevector simulator to remove finite-shot effects; chi-square and KS statistics computed

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Adam: generally convergent with isolated high-quality spikes; SPSA: faster convergence but degraded accuracy

speedup_claims.caveats: Paper studies accuracy/training-time trade-offs and does not claim a quantum speedup; it explicitly notes no proven asymptotic advantage.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: cq_load = n(k+1)+1; cq_gen_train = C_optimizer * s * cq_gen_eval for SPSA, or C_Adam * [n(k+1)] * s * cq_gen_eval for Adam; cq_train = j*b*(cq_gen_train + cq_discr_train)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: cc_discr_eval = nH1 + H1H2 + H2; cc_train = j*b*(cc_gen_train + cc_discr_train)
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: C_optimizer, s, j, b as defined in paper
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_classical: network-size-dependent factors in cc_discr_eval and optimizer-dependent constants C_optimizer

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: not applicable; study focuses on training behavior and accuracy of qGAN circuits with 3–4 qubits rather than demonstrating computational speedup
limiting_factors: training performed only on noiseless simulators
